answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it earns reputation, then slash that stake when independent audits confirm fraud. Reputation accrues only across a long horizon of useful work, so an attacker cannot cheaply mint trusted accounts just by registering them. A prism of randomly selected peers can review claims, while a plume of linked accounts sharing funding or behavior triggers closer checks. Sybils remain possible, but the attacker must tie up real capital and risk losing it.
